findings: Workbench previously completed frontend dependency installation/build before creating the native login process.
Backend startup eagerly imported CP-SAT/pandas even before any scheduling request.
Existing log measured 35.24 seconds between local_service_start and local_service_ready; its complete cause is not established by the import sample.
changes: Verify selected source, then start its real native login before asset preparation when that exact source supports the readiness contract. Older sources retain synchronous preparation.
Preserve source/frontend hashing, remote branch selection, profile locations, credential namespaces, canonical identity and TLS configuration.
Asset readiness gates frontend-dependent actions and local service startup, never supplies authentication authority. Failure, timeout and account-generation cancellation fail closed.
Use lightweight login shell import; defer CP-SAT until solving; show elapsed local-service preparation and record backend import/lifespan boundaries.
Skip redundant object fetch only when the remotely selected exact commit is already present locally.

user_observations: After integration, latest-development launch should show query/preparation status immediately, then native login before a cold frontend build finishes.
After login, service preparation should show elapsed time; main UI still waits for the verified account's healthy local service.
Repeat launch should retain the same profile and reuse only verified exact-source/frontend caches.
